original_card.question: Can a changed query demand or caller remove real work while satisfying native chronology and restoration?
methods: Construct and independently check one source-bound instance of the stated first experiment.
Seek an exact counterexample or target-specific complete-budget obstruction to that same proposed change.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A source-bound arbitrary-input identity and legal producer/consumer boundary with the complete paid and productive target invoice, including restoration, ownership, native alignment and extra charges. Price under the actual current model; historical ceiling.py assumptions must be established before use. A favorable optimistic relaxation keeps a route open but is not a completed supplier. A scoped local result remains useful; expansion requires the family-level budget gate.

actual_scope: Replace the odd-denominator five-point Toom-3 interpolation by a Gaussian-dyadic square evaluation, prove sharp integral-evaluation denominator height, and emit a five-product word preserving six inputs and arbitrary dirty outputs while restoring two initially clean fields.
scope_change_reason: This is a new algebraic bilinear interface, rather than an edit to the selected linear caller. PR3974 poses a missing Toom embedding; PR3992 excludes its first same-width candidate. This side result removes an arithmetic denominator without claiming either embedding or complete supplier acceptance.
bottleneck_link: A conditional bilinear replacement needs a legal coefficient ring and full restoration. Gaussian-dyadic interpolation eliminates the odd divisor 3 in the retained Toom screen, but does not supply an actual selected-provider sub-tensor or its physical invoice.
stop_rule: Stop after the first exact denominator improvement and full restoring word. Do not search for larger Toom blocks or claim the excluded PR3992 boundary is repaired.
evidence: PROOF.md proves the five-product identity, dirty-output restoration, exact Gaussian divisions, optimal pi denominator height within integral point-evaluation schemes, and the usual five-product bilinear lower bound. The standalone checker constructs an independent rational inverse, checks all 25 entries and both literal matrix transforms, all 46 tensor/dirty columns, 988 complete endpoint fixtures, all 69 instruction omissions, five invalid entrances and an inexact-division control.
